newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka editor gets suspended sentence for defamation.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka editor gets suspended sentence for defamation.

text.p: A Sri Lanka judge on Tuesday gave a suspended sentence of one year to the editor of a local weekend newspaper for criminal defamation of President Chandrika Kumaratunga.
Sinha Ratnatunga, editor of the Sunday Times, was found guilty of defaming Kumaratunga in an article published in the newspaper in 1995.

Colombo High Court Judge Upali de Z. Gunewardena also gave a suspended sentence of six months to Ratnatunga for violating certain sections of the Press Council Law of Sri Lanka, which deal with publication of incorrect information.
The verdict in the trial, which lasted 75 days, was read out in the court packed with journalists, lawyers and politicians.

The judge also fined Ratnatunga 7,500 rupees ($129) on the first count and 2,500 rupees ($43) on the second and said he would be liable to a total of seven months of imprisonment if he defaulted on the fines.

The case was brought against Ratnatunga after Kumaratunga complained to police that the article, which said she attended a late night birthday party of a parliament deputy, was defamatory. Kumaratunga said she never attended the party.
